canonical_families.label: Skill-rank-derived (skillinfo/TOTALRANK)
canonical_families.proof_width: Covers any formula segment containing the `skillinfo(` call or a bare `TOTALRANK` reference. Does not cover skill-rank use inside a `.MOD`-continuation row this script's join never reaches (see module docstring 'Extraction method'), and does not distinguish class-skill vs. cross-class skillinfo variants.

canonical_families.label: classlevel(...)-derived
canonical_families.proof_width: Covers any formula segment calling `classlevel(`. Known corpus defect (MEASURE-TWICE.md §3, `defects.md` D2): `classlevel()` does not verify its class-name argument, so a unit landing here is not automatically safe to bank through the interpreter until D2 is fixed -- this script only classifies the shape, it does not certify the value.

canonical_families.label: Level-threshold step-count (summed >= indicators)
canonical_families.proof_width: Narrow heuristic: >=2 `if(` calls AND >=2 numeric `>=` comparisons AND a top-level `+` in the same formula segment. Does not cover a step-count expressed across multiple separate DEFINE/BONUS tokens summed by the consumer rather than within one formula string -- that shape is invisible to a per-token classifier and would need a per-record aggregation pass.

canonical_families.label: Clamped/capped per-level scaling (min/max/floor/ceil around a level expr)
canonical_families.proof_width: Covers `min(`/`max(`/`floor(`/`ceil(` wrapping a formula segment that also contains a `<Word>LVL` term. Does not cover a clamp wrapping a named-counter variable with no literal LVL token in the same segment (e.g. a clamp on an accumulator whose own LVL dependency lives in a separate DEFINE row) -- that case falls through to F4 or F8 below, undercounting F5 by construction.

canonical_families.label: Per-level scaling (<Class>LVL bare or arithmetic)
canonical_families.proof_width: Covers any formula segment containing a `<Word>LVL` token, bare or inside arithmetic. Does not distinguish a modelled class's own LVL variable from an unmodelled class's (T2a/T12 overlap, `epic-breakdown.md` 'What the measurement actually established') -- that distinction needs the class roster, which this script does not consult.

canonical_families.label: Conditional-step (if/boolean toggle)
canonical_families.proof_width: Covers any formula segment containing an `if(` call not already claimed by F9/F6/F10 above. Does not distinguish a genuine boolean toggle from an `if(...)` used purely for a units-safe default (e.g. `if(hasfeat,X,0)` vs. a real branch) -- both read as the same shape to a regex-level classifier.

canonical_families.label: Ability-modifier-derived (STR/DEX/CON/INT/WIS/CHA)
canonical_families.proof_width: Covers a formula segment that is a bare ability abbreviation (optionally signed/offset) or contains one as a token. Does not cover an ability score referenced only by its long PCGen variable form (e.g. a custom-named stat-derived variable one level removed) -- that shape falls through to F4/F8.

canonical_families.label: Named-counter/pool variable (plain identifier reference)
canonical_families.proof_width: Covers a formula segment that is exactly one bare identifier (no arithmetic, no literal) and is not an ability abbreviation -- the shape `bonus_stack_reader.rs`'s binding-layer pattern targets (`technical-design.md` Gate 2). Does not cover a counter referenced inside arithmetic (`Counter+2`) -- that reads as F8 residual here, which undercounts F4 relative to a full producer-chain resolution (the 77.2%/893-of-1,156 figure in `epic-breakdown.md` Epic 1 comes from resolving producer chains, a heavier analysis than this per-formula classifier performs).

canonical_families.label: Flat-constant magnitude (bare literal)
canonical_families.proof_width: Covers a formula segment that is exactly a signed/unsigned integer or decimal literal, optionally with a trailing `%`. Does not cover a literal embedded in a larger arithmetic expression (e.g. `2+CON` is F3, not F1, by design -- the point of this family per `epic-breakdown.md` is that it 'gets zero benefit from any shared function', which only holds for bare literals).

canonical_families.label: No formula content (no DEFINE/BONUS token found for this unit)
canonical_families.proof_width: Covers a unit whose (book, source_file, source_line) join finds either no corpus record, or a corpus record whose data.raw_tokens carries no DEFINE/BONUS-prefixed key. Does not distinguish 'this unit genuinely has no computable magnitude' (a race description, a pure-text feat) from 'the join failed to find the record it should have' -- the `join_status` field on each ledger row (`no_record` vs `no_formula_tokens`) is what a reviewer checks to tell those apart; F0's own count does not.

canonical_families.label: Other named-variable expression (residual)
canonical_families.proof_width: Covers any non-empty formula segment that matched none of F1/F2/F3/F4/F5/F6/F7/F9/F10 above -- e.g. multi-term arithmetic mixing several identifiers, or a PCGen builtin this classifier does not recognise (var("..."), PREVARGTEQ-gated expressions, COUNT[...] terms). This is the classifier's own named blind spot per AT-32-G1-003 -- a non-zero F8 count is expected and does not indicate a defect by itself, but a cycle that finds F8 dominating a book's population should treat that as a signal the rule list needs another entry, not silence it.

mt_mapping.mt_label: Clamped/capped per-level scaling (min/max/floor wrapping a level expr)

mt_mapping.canonical_label: No formula content (no DEFINE/BONUS token found for this unit)
mt_mapping.note: No MT counterpart -- MT's ten families only ever partitioned the 4,948-unit formula-bearing subset; a unit with no DEFINE/BONUS token was never assigned to any MT family at all. F0 is the honest naming of that gap, not a new distinction MT lacked.
